slides.title: Give **"I don't know"** its own answer
slides.sub: A check with two answers will lie to you with one of them.
slides.scene: Corey the sprout sits as a quiz show contestant with three big buzzers in front of him instead of the usual one, looking delighted, while the other contestant, a grumpy cartoon robot, has only one buzzer and is sweating under the studio lights. Funny, bright.

slides.label: Before: two answers
slides.caption: Network hiccup? That's an **outage report**. Every time.
slides.scene: Corey the sprout in pyjamas is woken at night by a huge clanging alarm bell beside the bed; outside the window a single tiny cloud has passed over the moon. He looks exhausted and unimpressed, hair-leaves sticking up.

left.label: ❌ Two states
left.text: 0 pass, 1 fail. Not knowing gets folded into one of them.

right.label: ✅ Three states
right.text: 0 a run exists. 1 never tested. 2 I could not find out.

slides.caption: The exit code that says **"the checker is the problem"**, not the thing it checks.

slides.label: After
slides.caption: "Broken" and "couldn't tell" get **different responses**.
slides.scene: Corey the sprout calmly sorts envelopes into three neat pigeonholes at a post office counter, one with a green leaf sticker, one with a red leaf sticker, one with a big question-mark-shaped leaf; a queue of customers nods approvingly. Bright, tidy, funny.

slides.text: Systems that can't say "I don't know" will say something else. Usually the reassuring thing.
slides.save: 💾 Save this for your next health check
